definition: In models such as BERT, the CLS token is added to the beginning of each input example and is used as the aggregate representation for classification tasks.
details: In models such as BERT, the CLS token is added to the beginning of each input example and is used as the aggregate representation for classification tasks.

explainer.lead: The CLS token is a special marker placed at the start of an input in models such as BERT. Its output representation gives a classifier one place to look for information about the whole input, rather than a single word.

tiers.eli5: Imagine putting a blank summary card at the front of a stack of notes before asking someone to read them. After reading, they fill in that card with the important overall message. BERT uses the CLS token in a similar way when it needs to classify a whole piece of text.
tiers.practitioner: In a BERT-based classifier, prepend [CLS], run the sequence through the encoder, and pass the output at position 0 to the classification head. Train that head and, when fine-tuning, the encoder so this position learns an aggregate representation. Do not confuse it with the first ordinary token or assume it is the pooling method used by every model.
tiers.paperLevel: For tokens x1,...,xn, construct the sequence ([CLS], x1,...,xn) and encode it to obtain hidden states h_CLS,h1,...,hn. A classification head uses h_CLS as the aggregate input representation, commonly written y_hat = f(h_CLS). This convention is used in BERT; it defines an aggregation point, not a guarantee that every relevant detail is preserved.

explainer.example: For the review “This film was moving,” the input begins “[CLS] This film was moving.” After BERT processes it, the vector at the [CLS] position is passed to a sentiment classifier, which could predict “positive.”

usedIn.name: BERT
usedIn.detail: Places CLS at the start of each input example.

usedIn.name: Text classification
usedIn.detail: Uses the CLS output as input to a label predictor.

usedIn.name: Document classification
usedIn.detail: Provides one representation for classifying an entire input passage.

explainer.intuition: A classifier needs a single representation for an entire example, even though the encoder processes many tokens. CLS reserves one position whose output can gather and carry that example-level information.
howItWorks: Place the special CLS token before the input tokens.
Run the complete sequence through a model such as BERT.
Read the output representation at the CLS position.
Feed that representation to a classifier to predict a label.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives BERT-based classifiers a consistent interface between variable-length token sequences and a fixed label prediction. The same position can serve as the aggregate representation across training examples.
misconceptions: CLS is not itself the predicted class label; it is an input marker with an output representation.
Its output is not the representation of the first ordinary word.
It should not be assumed that every model uses CLS for pooling or classification.
